[b]TLDR:[/b] If you are into Flash-era nostalgia and enjoy simple but satisfying combat, Swords & Souls feels great for a while. However, the grind and endless mode, especially for achievement hunters, eventually make it more of a chore than a comfort game.


[h3][b]Full Thoughts[/b][/h3]

[b][i]Positive Points:[/i][/b]

[b]Aesthetic & Vibe -[/b] The game nails that nostalgic Flash game feel in a really charming way. It looks and sounds like something from that era in the best possible sense, which gives the whole experience a warm, familiar tone.

[b]Combat & Story -[/b] The main story combat is surprisingly fun, with lots of abilities to play around with and fights that actually make you think a bit despite the simple presentation. On top of that, the story has genuine heart, which helps pull you through the campaign.

[b][i]M

Fun game, I liked its gameplay loop. Also I liked its Paper Mario style hybrid of idle-battler and turn-based combat.

It really flared my arthritis, so I had to return it, but otherwise I would have kept it.

<3

This game is fundamentally good, the story is engaging, and the characters feel lively and well-written. I especially enjoyed the mini-games at the dojo. However, trying to reach Soulmaster rank in all missions for the related achievement becomes extremely tedious. It takes several hours without offering a significant increase in challenge or variety, you just repeat the same tasks over and over again.

The same applies to the achievement “Complete endless stage 120” There’s barely any real skill involved, it’s mostly a numbers game. Reaching that stage feels like a pure time sink, with nothing new or interesting to see or do anymore.

So, while the game itself is definitely worth playing, I wouldn’t recommend going for 100% completion solely for the achievements.

The main story? Fun. Nostalgic to anyone who played the old flash games, and still has that vibe.

That said, the endgame is a mess - a ton of achievements are tied to the tower mode, but there's zero balancing going on. It awards you gold for clearing, which is a currency that has zero use by the time you get there. The game grinds to a screeching halt, frustratingly, when it could have been very easy to keep scaling the training upgrades up via gold to make it less of a grind.

If you played the original flash game, and loved it as much as I did, then this game is an absolute treat. It carries every bit of charm and fun from the first game, while providing more content and expanding on previous features. There's way more of a story, the mainline game is longer, training is far more elaborate, and there are a bunch of other new features that make this one feel like even more than a deluxe version of its predecessor.

My only gripe for 100%ing the game would be how grindy it is to complete all the training achievements, but that's really only if you feel like it. Even if you never played the original, I would still recommend this game. You can complete the main story and do a bit more completionist stuff in under 10 hours, and there's some post-game content to keep you occupied as well.
